tips.title: Morning Sun Exposure
tips.text: Open the windows or step outside for 2 minutes to soak in natural light. It helps reset your circadian rhythm and boosts your mood for the day ahead.

tips.title: 1-Minute Morning Reset
tips.text: Before getting out of bed, take 3 deep breaths and repeat: "I am capable, resilient, and ready for today."

tips.title: Stay Hydrated
tips.text: Put a water bottle next to your feeding chair and take a sip every time baby latches or you sit down to rest.

tips.title: Morning Nausea Relief
tips.text: Keep plain crackers or rusk on your nightstand to eat a few bites before sitting up out of bed.

tips.title: Quick Confidence Boost
tips.text: Take 2 minutes to wash your face with cool water, brush your hair, or put on a fresh shirt to feel instantly refreshed.

tips.title: 3-Second Posture Drop
tips.text: Drop your shoulders away from your ears, unclench your jaw, and take a long slow breath out.

tips.title: 2-Minute Fresh Air
tips.text: Step outside the front door or open a window to pull in fresh air and reset your mood instantly.

tips.title: The Midday Hydration & Snack Refuel
tips.text: Grab a high-protein snack and finish a glass of water to beat the 2:00 PM energy slump.

tips.title: Upper Back Relief Stretch
tips.text: Roll your shoulders back and tilt your head gently side-to-side to release upper-back and neck tension that builds through the day.

tips.title: Unburdening Reset
tips.text: Hand off the baby for 5 minutes and stretch your arms overhead and take that moment for yourself.

tips.title: Elevate & Unwind
tips.text: Prop your feet up on two pillows for 10 minutes to relieve pressure, reduce swelling, and rest your lower back.

tips.title: Screen-Free Micro-Nap
tips.text: Put your phone face down, feet up, and close your eyes for 5 minutes to give your brain a quick recharge.

tips.title: Baby-Holding Relief
tips.text: Take 30 seconds to circle your wrists and slowly roll your neck to release the strain of holding and rocking all day.

tips.title: Low-Pressure Outings
tips.text: If energy allows, step outside for a gentle 5-10 minute walk in the cooler evening air to clear your head and lift your spirits.

tips.title: Set Gentle Boundaries
tips.text: Give yourself full permission to say "not right now" to visitors when your battery feels drained.

tips.title: Dim the Lights Early
tips.text: Lower your home's overhead lighting 1-2 hours before bedtime to signal to your brain (and baby's) that nighttime is approaching.

tips.title: Presence Over Progress
tips.text: Caring for yourself and your baby is the work today. If nothing else gets done, your day was still a success.

tips.title: Nesting Prep Buffer
tips.text: Pick one small baby setup task to finish early in the evening, then step away and give yourself full permission to rest.

tips.title: Uninterrupted Break
tips.text: Tonight, ask your partner or support person to take the baby for 15 minutes so you can have a warm, uninterrupted shower.

tips.title: Hand Off the List
tips.text: If you have support, pass the remaining to-dos to them and go rest, your rest matters more than a clean counter.

tips.title: Silence Break
tips.text: Even 20 minutes of quiet - no tasks, no screens, no noise can restore more than you expect. Ask for that space if you can, or find it when baby next sleeps.

tips.title: Leg Swelling Drain
tips.text: Prop your legs up against a wall or high pillows for 5 minutes to instantly drain foot and leg swelling.

tips.title: Mindless Comfort
tips.text: Close your eyes and play a soothing song so your brain can completely switch off.

tips.title: Brain Dump Journaling
tips.text: Jot down tomorrow's to-dos or lingering worries on a notepad to clear your mind before closing your eyes.

tips.title: Over-Prep the Station
tips.text: Restock diapers, wipes, and feeding supplies at your primary feeding spot before you go to sleep so you aren't searching in the dark.

tips.title: Pillow Fortress Nesting
tips.text: Tuck a support pillow between your knees and under your bump to relieve hip strain before trying to fall asleep.

tips.title: Unwind Mindset
tips.text: Set down your phone and play a comfort show or familiar playlist that asks nothing of your brain.

tips.title: Brainpower Reset
tips.text: You've made a thousand micro-decisions today. Put on your favorite show or movie you've seen before and just breathe.

tips.title: Quiet Night Company
tips.text: You are not alone right now. Thousands of parents across the world are up feeding their babies with you.

tips.title: Low-Light Mode
tips.text: Keep lights low and soft during midnight feeds to help both you and baby drift back to sleep easily.

tips.title: The Quiet Hours
tips.text: There is no rush right now. The world is asleep, and this quiet bonding moment belongs just to you two.

tips.title: Midnight Water Sip
tips.text: Keep a water bottle right by your bed for a quick sip during late-night wakeups.

tips.title: One Feed at a Time
tips.text: Don't count how many hours of sleep are left. Focus only on this current feed, then rest.

tips.title: Midnight Position Shift
tips.text: If you find yourself watching the clock, try shifting your pregnancy pillow and taking 3 slow breaths to ease yourself back into rest.
